J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges 'The set of edges C_ij connecting a component of G[S] to a component of G[T] is a cut-set.' First-choice line 36 asserts exactly that: 'Claim: Cij is a cut-set.' Its active assumptions are line 14-15 (C = delta(S) for the partition V = S sqcup T), lines 18-21 (S_1..S_p the components of G[S], T_1..T_q the components of G[T]), line 24 (C_ij = the edges of C from S_i to T_j), line 35 (C_ij non-empty) and Definition 1 at lines 4-7 (a cut-set is delta(S') for a partition of V into two non-empty parts). Under those, line 36 asserts precisely the proposition attacked, and it is the load-bearing step for line 60's conclusion.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A complete finite witness: 'In a 4-cycle v1-v2-v3-v4-v1 with S={v1,v3} and T={v2,v4}, the set of edges between S_1={v1} and T_1={v2} is exactly the single edge (v1,v2), which is not a cut-set.' The graph, the partition, the two components and the resulting C_11 are all given explicitly.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact enumeration in scripts/P40_check.py. In C_4 with S = {v1,v3}, T = {v2,v4}: both parts are non-empty so Definition 1 applies and C = delta(S) is all four edges; G[S] has components {v1} and {v3} and G[T] has components {v2} and {v4} (the source's Step 1), so with S_1 = {v1}, T_1 = {v2} the set C_11 is exactly the single edge (v1,v2), as the response states. Enumerating delta(S') over all 14 non-trivial bipartitions of the 4 vertices gives cut-sets of sizes 2 and 4 only, and C_11 is not among them, so C_11 is not a cut-set under Definition 1; under Definition 2's stated equivalent it also fails, since deleting (v1,v2) leaves C_4 connected (1 component before and after). The witness therefore satisfies all the assumptions line 36 is asserted under and falsifies its conclusion. No witness was replaced and nothing was repaired.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response emits only the ranked labels ('0036','0034','0060'), the claim and the counterexample. It states no consequence - it does not assert that Theorem 1 at lines 12-13 is false (which would be the overreaching move here, since the theorem itself is a standard fact and only the proof's Step 3 is being attacked).
